title: Handoff sprintlet notes and latency triage
content:
Quick summary (afternoon -> evening handoff)

Context: Afternoon watch saw intermittent 95th/99th tail increases on hosted API proxy (us-west cluster) between 14:05–15:30 PDT. No full outages, but elevated client errors (HTTP 502/504) correlated with token spikes for a subset of customers using long-sequence models. Metrics returned to baseline after several mitigations; root cause likely a combination of kv-cache eviction pressure + scheduler backpressure during concurrent long-sequence batches.

This doc = shift log + triage notes + short runbook deltas to propose for follow-up sprint. Keep short, actionable items at top.

Immediate state (what to know for next shift)
- Service health: API proxy and serving runtime stable now; latency 95th ~ 380ms, 99th ~ 1.1s (normal: 95th ~ 250ms, 99th ~ 650ms) but trending down. No active pages.
- Open alerts: SRE-3421 (pagerduty) - assigned to Jenna (in progress) for KV-cache tuning; escalation not required.
- Customer impact: Minor increased error rate for ~6 customers flagged by CS. Tickets created and PR triage with customer success (CS ticket refs in JIRA comments).
- Recent actions performed: scaled serving pool +2 GPUs, applied temporary rate-limit increase for dedicated tier, rolled forward emergency config (eviction threshold -> -10% headroom), restarted proxy nodes sequentially in us-west-2.

Timeline (concise)
- 14:02 PDT: Alert triggered — proxy 5xx surge.
- 14:06 PDT: First on-call acknowledgement (Marisol). Began running initial diagnostics (logs, trace).
- 14:12 PDT: Observed alignment with long-sequence model requests; KV cache miss rate jumped from 8% -> 37% on node set a-*.
- 14:25 PDT: Scaled serving pool for the long-runway model (model-id: rwx-1.3b-longseq-v2) by +2 replicas; small drop in error volume.
- 14:40 PDT: Backpressure on scheduler observed: queue_depth spikes to ~3x. Enabled short-term batching cap to limit concurrent long requests.
- 15:05 PDT: Restarted 2 proxy nodes (rolling) that had heavy GC pauses; gc metrics normalized.
- 15:28 PDT: Error rate dropped to baseline; alert resolved at 15:35 PDT.

Key evidence & logs to review (for next shift)
- Traces: trace ids (sample) — trace:b3a7d1, trace:c9f2ee (linked in GH tracing dashboard).
- Proxy logs: /var/log/redwood/proxy/us-west-2/proxy-2028-05-11.log (lines ~13200-13540 show repeated 504s).
- Serving runtime metrics: grafana dashboard: infra/serving/kvcache-metrics (time window 14:00–15:30 PDT).
- Node-level GC: node a-3 and a-5 had prolonged GC pause events around 14:30 (see infra/alerts/gc-pauses).

Immediate followups (must be tracked in SRE board)
1) Runbook: add dedicated section for long-sequence workload triage (owner: Jenna, JIRA SRE-3478). Deliverable: 1-page checklist with short mitigation commands + thresholds. Due: 2028-05-18.
2) KV-cache tuning experiment: capture current eviction thresholds and run a 24h canary with +15% cache headroom on us-west long-seq nodes (owner: Omar). JIRA:SRE-3421 to track metrics and regression. Due: 2028-05-16.
3) Proxy restart policy: propose automated rolling restart of proxy pods after sustained GC pause >120s window (owner: Marisol). Draft PR: infra/#518 — add health-check augmentation. Due: 2028-05-20.
4) Customer outreach: CS follow-ups for the flagged customers + post-mortem note (owner: Jenna). Ensure customer-visible incident summary is non-technical and sent by 2028-05-13.

Proposed short runbook deltas (draft text to be copy/pasted into runbook)
- New section: "Long-sequence request surge"
  - Symptoms: sudden delta in kv-cache miss rate >20% vs baseline AND scheduler queue_depth >2x baseline AND >100 concurrent ongoing stream tokens for a given model shard.
  - Immediate steps:
    1) Check kv-cache hit/miss: grafana -> infra/serving/kvcache-metrics; if miss_rate > 20%, consider increasing cache headroom on affected shard by +10%-15%.
    2) Throttle concurrent long requests: run 'redwoodctl routing set-rate --model rwx-1.3b-longseq-v2 --concurrency 45' (example; confirm current concurrency values first).
    3) Scale serving pool: 'kubectl -n redwood scale deployment rwx-1.3b-longseq-v2 --replicas=<current+2>' and validate traffic distribution.
    4) Trace and attach sample traces: use tracing dashboard, collect up to 5 trace ids, paste into incident ticket.
  - Escalation: if errors persist for >30 minutes after steps 1-3, escalate to on-call infra/serving (pagerduty escalation policy level 2).

Operational commands we used (copyable)
- kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=proxy -o wide
- kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deployment/proxy-deployment --timeout=10m
- redwoodctl serving scale --model rwx-1.3b-longseq-v2 --replicas 6
- redwoodctl monitor tail --service=serving --start=2028-05-11T14:00:00Z --end=2028-05-11T15:30:00Z --query=kvcache.miss_rate
- journalctl -u redwood-proxy -S "2028-05-11 14:00:00" -U "2028-05-11 15:40:00" | grep "504" | sed -n '13200,13550p'

Notes / debugging observations that matter
- Long-sequence requests are highly correlated with increased KV cache churn — sequence length correlates with larger KV caches which increases eviction rate under tight memory.
- GC pauses on proxy nodes amplified tail latency; GC correlated with larger JS heaps in proxy due to trace logging spikes. We should throttle verbose trace logging for production proxy nodes by default.
- Batching policy config had permissive max-concurrent long requests; default should be more conservative for mixed workloads.

Outstanding decisions for planning meeting
- Default cache headroom for long-sequence models: +10% vs current 0%? (Impact on memory/cost vs fewer evictions).
- Should we enable automatic temporary concurrency caps per-model when kv-cache miss > X%? (automation vs manual intervention)
- GC mitigation plan: adjust JVM flags for proxy container or shift to a non-blocking GC mode; schedule perf bench before rolling.

Handoff checklist for next on-call
- [ ] Confirm SRE-3421 and SRE-3478 are assigned and have owners.
- [ ] Validate that the us-west long-seq canary (Omar) started correctly — check canary dashboard.
- [ ] Ensure proxy verbose tracing is reduced in prod config (PR opened: infra/#518) or note rollback if it causes issues.
- [ ] Pull the customer ticket list and confirm CS outreach timeline.
- [ ] Keep watch on 95th/99th latency for next 6 hours; if 99th > 2x baseline, page L2.

Retention notes (for post-incident writeup)
- Attach sample traces, diff of config before/after, and the sequence-length distribution histogram for model rwx-1.3b-longseq-v2.
- Collect HPA scaling events and controller logs during 14:00–15:30 window.

Misc (notes to self)
- Consider adding a synthetic traffic job that mimics 30–60s long-sequence sessions during off-peak to exercise KV-cache. Could reduce surprises.
- Quick perf test idea: run a 2-hour canary with elevated sequence length at low QPS to isolate GC vs cache eviction effects.

Signed off for handoff: Sahil (afternoon watch).
If something looks urgent, ping oncall@sre and post to #sre-oncall with subject 'US-WEST longseq latency followup'.

Attachments to add to ticket: trace samples, proxy log extract (lines referenced), grafana snapshot (kvcache + scheduler queues), link to infra PR 518.

-- end of shift note --
